text:
You need a simple 1–3 page WordPress site for a personal trainer, with a secure client log-in area where members can access organized fitness videos and where you can easily update testimonials, services, and education content later.

Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne. I build full-stack websites and member portals, and I’d be a good fit for this because your project needs both a clean public-facing site and a flexible private area that’s easy for you to manage over time.

I’ve spent 7 years working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML, and CSS. While your site is on WordPress, the core needs here are the same ones I’ve handled in app and portal builds: organized content, reliable log-in access, and a structure that’s simple to maintain.

A relevant project was a booking platform for fitness studios for Pulsebox Studios. I built a white-label class booking app where each studio got its own subdomain, timetable, and memberships. One result from that build was 64 studios onboarded in 6 months. That project also reached a 71% checkout conversion, so I’m comfortable building user flows that are clear, structured, and conversion-friendly.

For your site, I’d approach it by keeping the public pages lean and polished, then setting up the member portal with clear headings or folders for different fitness topics. Since your videos are already on Loom, embedding them into the right sections should be straightforward. I’d also make sure the content areas are easy for you to edit later, so you can change testimonials, services, and membership content without needing a rebuild each time.

In terms of timing, a project like this would typically take about 1–2 weeks depending on how quickly the page structure, membership rules, and content are finalized. Budget-wise, I’d estimate a moderate fixed-scope build, but I’d want to confirm the exact number of pages, the member access setup, and how much styling/customization you want before giving a firm figure.

If you’d like, I can help you keep the public site simple while making the member portal organized and easy to update. Would you like the log-in area to be open to all members with one shared password, or should each client have their own individual account?
